title: Open-source Shopify alternative: GoCommerce vs Shopify
description: Shopify vs GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce: platform fees per order, hosting, code ownership, apps and payments — and where Shopify is the better choice.
ogDescription: Rent a hosted platform, or run an open-source one yourself. Fees, ownership and trade-offs, sourced.
h1: Open-source Shopify alternative: GoCommerce vs Shopify
tagline: Shopify rents you a store. GoCommerce gives you one.
lede: Shopify runs the software and the servers and charges a monthly plan, plus a fee on every order taken through a third-party gateway. GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce are MIT source. Run them yourself and there is no plan, no per-order fee, and every line of the checkout is yours to change — along with the server it runs on. Or start a store hosted on kitcommerce.store, which pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.

glanceLede: Each row is checkable: Shopify’s side against its own pricing and help pages, linked at the foot of this page; ours against the GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce pages on this site.
rows: What it is
A hosted platform. Shopify runs the software, the servers and the upgrades.
An open-source platform you run, in two MIT packages: a Go backend with its admin compiled in, and a SvelteKit storefront.
Software price
A monthly plan: Basic $29, Grow $89 or Advanced $359 a month billed yearly ($39, $105 or $399 month to month); Plus from $2,300 a month on a one- or three-year term.
Nothing to run it yourself; both packages are MIT licensed. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Fee on each order
2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, 0.6% on Advanced and 0.2% on Plus when a third-party gateway takes the payment; waived with Shopify Payments, and not charged on cash on delivery or other manual payments.
None when you run it yourself: your payment gateway’s own fee is the only one. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Hosting
Included in the plan.
Yours when you run it: one Go binary and one PostgreSQL database, on any server. Or hosted on kitcommerce.store, for {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
Source code
Closed. You extend it through apps, themes and APIs.
Open. Change anything, checkout included, and ship it under your own name.
Extensions
The Shopify App Store, where each app sets its own price.
51 modules — payments, shipping, messaging, search, feeds, MCP — each compiled in when you import it. No app store.
Payments
Shopify Payments in 41 countries and regions; third-party providers elsewhere, with the fee above.
Razorpay, Stripe, Cashfree, Adyen, Paddle, Hyperswitch and five more as modules; cash on delivery built in.
Storefront
Online Store themes, or Hydrogen for headless.
Svelte Commerce, server-rendered SvelteKit with 79 live demo themes — or any client that speaks HTTP.
Admin
Shopify’s admin, on the web and in its mobile app.
61 admin screens compiled into the GoCommerce binary, on the same API a storefront uses.
Your data
Exportable through CSV and the Admin API; the runtime is Shopify’s.
Rows in your own PostgreSQL, which you can query, back up and move.
Help when it breaks
Shopify’s own support team.
GitHub issues, discussions and Discord. No support contract.
Track record
Millions of merchants.
Svelte Commerce runs arialshop.com and other stores in production. GoCommerce has none yet.

cost.note: A worked example from Shopify’s US price list: $10,000 a month in sales through a third-party gateway on Basic pays Shopify $200 a month in third-party fees — 2% — on top of the $29 plan and the gateway’s own charge. The same sales on GoCommerce you run yourself pay the gateway alone; the server and the developer are the costs that replace that fee. On a store hosted on kitcommerce.store, the same sales pay {hostedFee} of each successful sale.

themWhen: You want a store live this week and there is no developer on the team.
You depend on particular apps from the Shopify App Store.
You would rather pay a monthly fee than own servers, backups and upgrades.
You sell where Shopify Payments is offered, so the per-order fee is waived.
usWhen: Shopify’s 1–2% of revenue on a third-party gateway costs more than a server and a developer’s time, and you would rather run the store yourself.
You want a store hosted for you: kitcommerce.store takes {hostedFee} of each successful sale.
You want the code — checkout, pricing, order flow — to be yours to change.
You sell in India, where Shopify Payments is not offered, so every plan pays that fee on online payments — cash on delivery and other manual payments are exempt.
You want B2B price lists, several storefronts or marketplace vendors without a higher plan.

move.title: Moving from Shopify, or not moving at all
paras: Two paths, and the second needs no migration.

Move the backend: GoCommerce’s import-shopify module brings a whole Shopify catalogue across in one go, matching on Shopify’s own product ids, so running it again updates rather than duplicates. A separate order importer loads your history without sending a single confirmation email or moving stock.

Or keep Shopify and change only the storefront: Svelte Commerce has a Shopify connector — 16 of the 27 services it applies to are wired, cart and checkout among them — so a SvelteKit storefront can front your existing Shopify store.

faq.a: For a store with a developer, it covers the core: catalogue, carts, checkout, orders, inventory across locations, discounts, customers, B2B price lists and channels, with an admin compiled in. What it does not replace is the part of Shopify you pay not to think about — hosting, upgrades, an app store and a support team.

The software is. GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce are MIT licensed, with no plan and no paid tier, and running them yourself carries no per-order fee. The server, the database and the time of whoever runs them are real costs, and for a small store they can exceed a Shopify plan. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale instead.

faq.q: Can I keep Shopify and use Svelte Commerce as the storefront?
faq.a: Yes. Svelte Commerce has a Shopify connector, with cart, checkout and sign-in wired. It is one of 26 backend connectors, and coverage for each is measured on the backends page rather than claimed.

faq.q: How do I move my catalogue from Shopify?
faq.a: With the import-shopify module, which imports a whole Shopify catalogue and matches on Shopify’s own product ids, so a second run updates rather than duplicates. An order importer brings history across without firing events or moving stock.

faq.q: Is there a hosted version, like Shopify?
faq.a: Yes. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale. Running both packages yourself, on your own server or a developer’s, stays free.

faq.q: Why does Shopify charge a fee on my own payment gateway?
faq.a: Shopify’s pricing charges a third-party transaction fee — 2%, 1%, 0.6% or 0.2% by plan — whenever a provider other than Shopify Payments takes the payment. Where Shopify Payments is available and used as the only provider, the fee is waived.
